# Validating the detection ideas on real data (IEEE-CIS)

*Generated by `python -m src.ieee.validate` on 2026-11-18 from the IEEE-CIS train set:
590,540 transactions, base fraud rate 3.50%. The data itself is not in this repo
(competition rules: non-commercial use, no redistribution); only these aggregate results are.*

The simulator's detectors are tuned on synthetic data, so this checks whether the **underlying signals**
carry information on real, labelled e-commerce fraud. Each idea is mapped to its closest proxy in the
anonymized IEEE-CIS columns (header of `sql/ieee/signals.sql`). Lift = fraud rate when the signal fires
÷ overall fraud rate; above 1 means the signal is informative.

## 1. First pass: signals as designed, before looking at the data

| signal | share of txns | fraud rate when present | lift | share of fraud covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New device for a known customer | 3.8% | 7.6% | 2.18x | 8.4% |
| Micro amount (< $5) | 0.2% | 6.2% | 1.76x | 0.4% |
| Card first seen today (D1 = 0) | 47.4% | 4.2% | 1.20x | 57.1% |
| Amount > 3x customer's earlier average | 2.9% | 4.1% | 1.18x | 3.4% |
| Card velocity (3+ txns on the card in the previous hour) | 15.0% | 4.0% | 1.13x | 16.9% |
| Buyer and recipient email domains differ | 4.0% | 2.9% | 0.82x | 3.3% |
| Anonymous / privacy email domain | 6.4% | 2.6% | 0.76x | 4.8% |

- **Transferred (lift ≥ 1.5x):** *New device for a known customer*, *Micro amount (< $5)*
- **Weak (1.0 to 1.5x):** *Card first seen today (D1 = 0)*, *Amount > 3x customer's earlier average*, *Card velocity (3+ txns on the card in the previous hour)*
- **Did not transfer (below 1x):** *Buyer and recipient email domains differ*, *Anonymous / privacy email domain*

Combined score (fixed weights, not fitted): ROC AUC **0.553** (0.5 = random).

*The score is a sum of a few binary signals, so it takes only a handful of distinct values and a "top 1%"
cut falls inside large groups of tied transactions (ties are broken by transaction id). AUC, which handles
ties properly, is the number to trust; the precision/recall cut-offs are indicative.*

| alert budget | precision | recall |
|---|---|---|
| top 1% of txns | 2.6% | 0.7% |
| top 5% of txns | 3.5% | 5.0% |
| top 10% of txns | 4.4% | 12.6% |

## 2. Why some signals didn't transfer

Diagnostics on the same data showed the misses were **mapping errors**, not evidence against the ideas:

- **`card1` is not one card.** It has 13,553 distinct values, one shared by up to
  14,932 transactions, so "velocity on the same card1" measures popular card groups, not one
  card being hammered. Velocity per reconstructed customer is the right proxy.
- **`anonymous.com` is not a privacy service here.** It covers 36,998 transactions at a
  2.3% fraud rate (below the base rate), so it behaves like a mainstream provider.
  Actual privacy-focused providers are rare but far riskier (protonmail.com 41%,
  mail.com 19%).
- **The recipient-email risk is the reverse of the idea.** Fraud is 9.7% when a recipient email
  is present and *matches* the buyer's domain, 2.9% when it differs, and 2.1% when
  there is none. Having a recipient email at all is the risk signal.

## 3. Second pass: corrected proxies, tested on the latest 40% of transactions

The corrections were chosen after looking at the full data, so to limit self-deception they are reported
on the latest 40% of transactions by time (236,216 transactions, base rate
3.67%). That is the closest thing to fresh data this dataset allows, but it is
**not** a clean out-of-sample test, because the diagnostics above used every row.

| signal | share of txns | fraud rate when present | lift | share of fraud covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2: Privacy email provider (list without anonymous.com) | 0.1% | 23.3% | 6.34x | 0.7% |
| v2: Recipient email present | 19.8% | 10.2% | 2.76x | 54.7% |
| v2: Customer velocity (3+ txns by the reconstructed customer in the previous hour) | 2.6% | 7.6% | 2.07x | 5.3% |

On that holdout, the same fixed weights score ROC AUC **0.570** with the first-pass
signals and **0.666** with the corrected ones.

| alert budget | precision | recall |
|---|---|---|
| top 1% of txns | 11.2% | 3.0% |
| top 5% of txns | 10.8% | 14.7% |
| top 10% of txns | 9.7% | 26.5% |

## 4. What this means for the project

- The account-takeover idea (**new device on a known customer**) carries over directly and is the strongest
  first-pass signal; behavioural velocity carries over once it is measured per customer.
- Proxies matter as much as ideas: two of seven first-pass mappings pointed the wrong way because of what
  the anonymized columns actually mean. On a real team, the equivalent step is checking field definitions
  with data engineering before trusting a rule.
- A hand-weighted score of a few binary signals is a weak ranker on its own. These signals belong as features
  in a fitted model (with the dataset's C/D/V columns), with rules reserved for high-lift, explainable cases.
- Friendly fraud can't be tested here: `isFraud` is chargeback-based, so it mixes true and friendly fraud.
